cf.title: Add get_actual_variable_range index page read limit (complements existing VISITED_PAGES_LIMIT)

verdict_reasoning: The problem is real and agreed: Tom Lane confirmed it in message #2, and the demand angle found a production case. The one surviving objection, prior-attempts-1, is a fixable design point. INDEX_PAGES_LIMIT = 3 can end the probe where master finds the true endpoint, and no posted numbers measure how often. The objectors to the earlier design have not replied to the revised one, so a committer who knows the planner must judge that trade-off.

brief.title: Limit leaf page reads in get_actual_variable_range with INDEX_PAGES_LIMIT
brief.problem: The planner's get_actual_variable_range can read an unbounded number of index leaf pages when many index tuples are marked LP_DEAD, because VISITED_PAGES_LIMIT counts only heap page visits. Queue-like tables, such as those in Mark Callaghan's insert benchmark and possibly TPC-C's order table, suffer high planning latency as a result.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds INDEX_PAGES_LIMIT, set to 3, which counts leaf pages that return zero matching items. The scan gives up when the count hits the limit, and the planner falls back to pg_statistic. VISITED_PAGES_LIMIT stays as is, and only nbtree's _bt_readnextpage counts pages, so the first leaf page read is never counted.
user_visible_surface: C API: new scan descriptor field in relscan.h, named xs_index_pages_limit in an earlier version, that callers set to ask the index AM to stop early.
No SQL, GUC, catalog or protocol change.
author_claims: For the earlier single-leaf-page design, EXPLAIN latency with 20% deleted tuples was about 10 times lower than master, with no change when there are no dead tuples.
With the new limit, standbys keep today's behavior, because LP_DEAD bits are not set or used there and each page usually returns a match.
Counting only in _bt_readnextpage adds no overhead to simple point queries.
Reading more than a few empty leaf pages at the end of the index indicates a pathological case, so reading more pages is unlikely to find a value.
The patch no longer depends on the index prefetching work, because the slot-based table AM index scan interface is now committed.
brief.thread_state: Tom Lane objected to the first single-page design and Andres Freund doubted index cost as a proxy for heap cost; the author then changed to the complementary limit. Neither has replied to the revised design, and Rui Zhao is listed as reviewer with no review posted.
unclear: The thread has no benchmark numbers for the v1 design; all posted numbers are for the earlier single-page design.
The proposal does not say how often get_actual_variable_range now fails to get an estimate, which is Tom Lane's main concern.
The proposal does not say how the value 3 was chosen.
The proposal does not say what happens with index AMs other than nbtree.
The proposal does not say whether the fix is meant for back branches.

objections.title: Revised limit still gives up early, and no failure-rate data answers message #2
objections.failure_scenario: A batch insert at the high end of a timestamp index rolls back on a unique conflict. Later planning calls kill those entries and find more than three leaf pages with no live items. The planner falls back to a stale pg_statistic maximum. Range queries on recent rows get underestimated, and the DBA sees a bad plan with no sign of the cause.
objections.argument: In message #2, Tom Lane rejected the single-page design for its higher chance of getting no estimate, and suggested a limit of about a thousand dead entries. Message #7 gave the rollback case above. INDEX_PAGES_LIMIT counts empty pages, so three sparse pages holding a few dead entries trigger it as easily as three full ones. Message #8 argues the case is short-lived, but neither objector replied to v1, and all posted numbers are for the earlier design.
objections.author_must_show: With INDEX_PAGES_LIMIT = 3, how often does get_actual_variable_range return no estimate in the rollback and queue cases where master finds the true endpoint?

critic.reasoning: The limit counts leaf pages with zero matching items, so a rolled-back batch spanning a few leaf pages can end the probe where master finds the endpoint. Message #8's answer covers only workloads that retry, and no posted numbers measure the revised design.

refuted.title: Existing range queries can lose actual-endpoint estimates with no way back
refuted.failure_scenario: On a primary, a batch insert of a few thousand rows at the high end of a key rolls back, and a later planner probe marks those entries LP_DEAD. Today the next probe walks past them cheaply and finds the real max. With the patch it stops after 3 empty leaf pages and falls back to the stale pg_statistic max, so `where id > $recent` gets a near-zero row estimate and a bad plan.
refuted.argument: Andres Freund described this case in message #7 and noted that inserts are where stale stats give the worst estimates. Message #8 answers that retries will soon refill the end of the index, but that only applies to workloads that retry, and nobody replied to the revised design. Posted numbers cover only the earlier design, and no numbers show how often endpoint lookups now fail. Users get no setting to restore today's behaviour. Message #4 raised the same point, and the proposal does not say whether back branches would get this change.
refuted.author_must_show: In workloads without a queue pattern, such as rolled-back batch inserts, how often does INDEX_PAGES_LIMIT now make get_actual_variable_range fall back to pg_statistic, compared with master?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which states the same rollback scenario and the same missing failure-rate data. The added points about a setting and back branches name no separate failure.

refuted.title: Scan-descriptor limit has an nbtree-only contract that can drop silently
refuted.failure_scenario: A later rework of nbtree scans, such as the amgetbatch prefetching work, moves page reads out of _bt_readnextpage and the new limit stops being counted. Ordinary tests and benchmarks stay green. Queue-table users see planning latency rise again after an upgrade, and nobody notices until a field report arrives.
refuted.argument: The patch adds a generic field in relscan.h, but only nbtree's _bt_readnextpage honors it, and other ordered index AMs ignore it with no error. Message #5 and message #12 say the prefetching work will keep reshaping this code. Nothing in the proposal makes a forgotten counter fail loudly. The author knows nbtree well, which lowers the risk but does not define the contract for other AMs or future scan paths.
refuted.author_must_show: What documented index AM contract and regression test make the leaf-page limit fail visibly if a future nbtree scan path or another ordered AM stops honoring it?

critic.reasoning: An index AM or scan path that ignores the field behaves as master does today, so no new failure arises, and the patch comment shows the committed xs_visited_pages_limit follows the same pattern. The patch was carried inside the prefetching series through v28, by the same author.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a scan descriptor field in relscan.h that only nbtree honors.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: get_actual_variable_range falls back to pg_statistic after three empty leaf pages, which changes row estimates for existing queries.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The proposal does not say whether back branches get the fix, and the relscan.h struct change would need an ABI-safe form there.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A second hard-coded limit, counted only in _bt_readnextpage, must survive later reworks of nbtree scans.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The patch adds counting in _bt_readnextpage, which every nbtree scan that moves to a next leaf page runs.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: With INDEX_PAGES_LIMIT = 3, how often does get_actual_variable_range return no estimate in the rollback and queue cases where master finds the true endpoint?
What are the planning latency numbers for the v1 design, since all posted numbers are for the earlier single-leaf-page design?
How was the value 3 chosen, and how do failure rate and latency change with a larger value?
Why does the limit count empty leaf pages instead of dead index entries skipped, as message #2 suggested with a threshold of about a thousand?
Is the fix meant for back branches, and if so, how does the relscan.h field change stay ABI-safe there?

committability.owner_note: Peter Geoghegan wrote the patch and works in nbtree; Tom Lane took part in message #2. Someone who knows selfuncs.c and planner estimation should agree to the estimate-loss trade-off.
committability.liability: The owner signs for plan regressions when the probe gives up early and the planner uses a stale pg_statistic endpoint. That lasts as long as the hard-coded limit exists.
committability.author_follow_up: The author changed the design after the objections in the thread and posted v1 in message #12, which suggests continued work.

priority.reason: Queue-like tables are common, and the thread shows a published benchmark and a production report. The patch is small, adds no SQL or GUC surface, and needs failure-rate numbers for the revised design before commit.

provisional_note: No code was read. Whether the counter covers all nbtree scan paths (backward scans, parallel scans, array keys) and adds no cost for ordinary scans could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

This reverts commit aa607980aee08416211f003ab41aa750f5559712.

This test proved to be unstable on the buildfarm, timing out before the
standby could catch up on 32-bit machines where more rows were required
and failing to reliably trigger multiple index vacuum rounds on 64-bit

Because the instability is only known to be present on versions of

being reverted on master and REL_17_STABLE.

As having this coverage may be valuable, there is a discussion on the
thread of possible ways to stabilize the test. If that happens, a fixed
test can be committed again.

precedents_retrieved.title: Full support for index LP_DEAD hint bits on standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let index scans on a hot standby use and set index LP_DEAD hint bits, which are currently ignored during recovery. The first design added a WAL record carrying a hint-bit xmin horizon tied to hot_standby_feedback; it was later reworked to mask primary-set hint bits in full-page images and let the standby set its own bits only when minRecoveryPoint makes it safe.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Late in the cycle Peter Geoghegan reviewed the patch; his review is visible only as quoted in the author's reply. He questioned whether the lockless algorithm using pg_memory_barrier() was correct, pointed out a problem with LP_DEAD bits on posting lists during posting list splits, and said the patch had serious design flaws. In his visible message he said the area carries a real risk of hidden data corruption bugs, that few committers could evaluate such a patch, and that the problem needed better explanation. A test added by the patch was also failing intermittently, and the author moved the entry back to Waiting on Author.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
You must understand that this whole area is *scary*. The potential for
serious data corruption bugs is very real.

precedents_retrieved.title: Adjust tuples estimate for appendrel
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets an appendrel's tuples estimate to the sum of the tuples of its live child relations instead of to its rows estimate. This lets estimate_num_groups() apply the formula from 84f9a35e3 to appendrels, which reduces the over-estimate of distinct groups that made the planner under-cost incremental sort.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Andrei Lepikhov supported committing the patch but asked for a regression test that checks the appendrel->tuples change directly, and the author had said he could not devise one. After that the discussion moved to wider ndistinct estimation ideas, and no later message from the author is shown.

This reverts commit eafdf9de06e9b60168f5e47cedcfceecdc6d4b5f
and its back-branch counterparts.  Corey Huinker pointed out that
we'd discussed this exact change back in 2016 and rejected it,
on the grounds that there's at least one usage pattern with LIMIT
where an infinite endpoint can usefully be used.  Perhaps that
argument needs to be re-litigated, but there's no time left before

demonstrating the usage with LIMIT.  That'll at least remind us of
the issue if we forget again.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove page-read callback from XLogReaderState
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the page-read callback (and later the open and close segment callbacks) from XLogReaderState. XLogReadRecord becomes a state machine that returns XLREAD_NEED_DATA, and the caller then loads WAL pages itself.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Thomas Munro committed a squashed version in April 2021, and it was later reverted. The author's note mentions a possible defect on one platform but does not give the cause. In September 2021 Thomas Munro pointed the author to a message from Andres Freund that the author had not seen and had not yet answered, and the entry was then returned with feedback. The visible messages do not show the content of that message or the exact reason for the revert.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve join selectivity estimation using extended statistics
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch uses per-table extended statistics, mainly functional dependencies, when it estimates join selectivity in clausesel.c. It also tries to combine join clauses with relation-level filters in calc_joinrel_size_estimate to estimate conditional probabilities.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra found the design at the wrong level of abstraction. Clausesel.c handled extended statistics directly, dependencies were applied clause by clause in a fixed order and only on the inner relation, and he proposed handling all join clauses for a pair of relations at once in extended_stats.c. The author agreed it could be done better but posted no new version. In July the patch no longer compiled, and it still did not one commitfest later, so it was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use ReadRecentBuffer() for btree root page
precedents_retrieved.summary: Cache the btree root page's buffer ID per relation and use ReadRecentBuffer() in _bt_getroot() to skip the buffer mapping lookup. To make that scale, ReadRecentBuffer() would pin with PinBuffer() instead of taking the buffer header spinlock, which also bumps the usage count.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected to keeping the cached root buffer in rd_amcache, because each access method would then duplicate the same code. He suggested putting the fields in RelationData instead. Thomas Munro answered with an experimental LRU of recent lookups, and Andres said that should be a separate facility. No revised patch followed, so in January 2024 the entry was set to Waiting on Author, and the visible messages show no reply after that.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am wondering if we don't want something more generic than stashing this in rd_amcache.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoiding plan disasters with LIMIT
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Avoiding plan disasters with LIMIT
Threads: Yet another abort-early plan disaster on 9.3

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found in the index. The thread names commit 9c6ad5eaa9, which added VISITED_PAGES_LIMIT, as background (messages #1 and #4). Message #4 calls it a quick backpatchable fix, which this patch extends rather than reverses.
The proposal adds no SQL, GUC, catalog, dump or psql surface, so the only compatibility concern from this angle is the planner behaviour change for existing queries.

The patch changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog or wire protocol. It adds only a scan descriptor field in relscan.h, which is a normal change on master. On a hot standby, LP_DEAD bits are not used, so as message #9 says the new limit rarely triggers there and behaviour stays as today. The nbtree VACUUM bookkeeping invariant does not apply, because the patch does not change VACUUM. If the fix is later proposed for back branches, the relscan.h struct change would need an ABI-safe form, but the proposal does not ask for a backpatch.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It adds an internal limit on leaf page reads during planner endpoint probes, with no new SQL, GUC, catalog, role or protocol surface, and it lowers rather than raises the work an unprivileged user can trigger by planning a query.

From the maintenance angle the cost looks small: there is no GUC, catalog or SQL surface, and the extra work sits in _bt_readnextpage only. The nbtree VACUUM invariant does not apply because this is a planner-time scan. The author is the committer who owns the area.

I found no existing Postgres feature, setting or extension that bounds leaf page reads in get_actual_variable_range, and the limit lives inside planner and nbtree code that no hook reaches. Aggressive vacuuming of queue tables only reduces how often the problem occurs, and the new limit extends VISITED_PAGES_LIMIT instead of adding a second way to do the same job.

The material shows real demand: Mark Callaghan's published benchmark, Tom Lane agreeing the problem exists (message #2), and Jakub Wartak's production case where planning took about 27 minutes (message #4). The patch has no user-visible surface, and the open questions are about how often estimates fail, which other angles cover.
